turns.user: why does my plan put protein in every single meal? can't I just have a big steak at dinner and be done
turns.reply:
You *could* hit all 130g of your protein in one giant meal, but spreading it across your day works much better for a couple of clear reasons.

First, your body is constantly repairing and rebuilding muscle tissue, especially while you're in a calorie deficit for fat loss. Muscle protein synthesis peaks when you get around 30–40g of protein in a sitting, so giving your body three or four steady hits throughout the day keeps that repair process turned on continuously rather than just once every 24 hours.

Second, it's pure practical appetite control. Protein is the most satiating macro you can eat. Spreading that 130g out across breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks keeps you full and stops energy dips between meals, which makes sticking to your 1660 calorie target a whole lot easier. 

That said, the total number at the end of the day is still what matters most. If you ever have a day where breakfast is lighter on protein, you can easily make up the difference at dinner — you don't need to stress over precise timing, but keeping it balanced across the day just makes life easier. 

Does the current spread feel like a lot to manage at breakfast or lunch, or were you just curious about the math behind it?
